unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.3 - THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will conduct an interview with a person who lives in a smart or slow city about leisure activities in pairs. They may choose a real person or create an avatar. If they like, they can videotape the interview. Then, they will report the interviews in the classroom. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as life in smart cities and slow cities; leisure activities in smart, slow and other different cities; challenges of planning life in the city for the future'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 11 of upper secondary school may know what life in smart cities and slow cities; leisure activities in smart, slow and other different cities; challenges of planning life in the city for the future mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 11 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 11 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as life in smart cities and slow cities; leisure activities in smart, slow and other different cities; challenges of planning life in the city for the future'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To describe challenges of planning life in the city for the future in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: City Planning Timeline: Predict the Future The teacher gives a scenario where students imagine they are urban planners designing a city for 2030 to solve problems like overpopulation, congestion, and contamination while improving infrastructure, mobility, and conservation. Students design a timeline with sentences such as, ''By 2025, the city will have constructed affordable housing'' or ''By 2030, urban planners will have been working on sustainable expansion for five years''. Each event must address a specific challenge by using the target vocabulary such as ''affordable, expansion, conservation, and mobility''. After completing their timelines, the students will present them to the class and explain their solutions. This activity encourages critical thinking and the use of target vocabulary and target grammar practice in a creative way. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, target grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe life in smart cities and slow cities in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Complete the Vision: City Life in 2030 The teacher provides a worksheet with incomplete sentences such as ''By 2030, the city will have improved its ________'' or ''By 2030, they will have reduced ________ in city centres'', by using the target words from the word bank (infrastructure, mobility, congestion, overpopulation, expansion, affordable, conservation). Examples include ''By the end of the next decade, new ________ solutions will have been introduced'' or ''People will have prioritised ________ of natural resources''. Digital Support: Students can use an online word bank on a tool, complete an interactive quiz on a tool to practice, and watch short videos or view pictures of smart cities for inspiration. They write and share sentences with peers or groups, by discussing the importance of these changes for future city planning. In the end, the teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
